transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aurelia Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Eng Mgr), Nadia Gomez (Sr Data Eng)

Auto-generated Summary: (may be imperfect) Discussed embeddings dimensionality, integration with Pinecone, hybrid BM25 + ANN reranking approach, and Dedicated vs Hosted deployment options. Action items agreed.

00:00 - 00:32 Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ethan with Redwood, and with me is Sofia our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:33 - 01:05 Priya: Hi Ethan, thanks, doing well. I'm Priya, head of ML at Aurelia. We also have Liam and Nadia on the call.
01:06 - 01:30 Liam: Hey, quick wave. We put together a brief agenda — we're evaluating options for moving our search + rerank pipeline off a prototype into production.
01:31 - 02:05 Sofia: Great, can you give us a quick overview of the current flow? We're especially interested in where embeddings are generated, what vector DB you're using, and throughput/latency expectations.
02:06 - 02:45 Priya: Sure. Right now embeddings are generated with OpenAI's ada-like embeddings (we might switch to 1536 later), storing vectors in Pinecone. Search pipeline is BM25 to get candidates then ANN rerank with cosine similarity. Peak QPS is about 80 qps during business hours, median latency target for rerank is sub-100ms ideally, 95th under 200ms.
02:46 - 03:10 Sofia: Okay good, that helps. A couple clarifying questions: are you doing offline batches to update indexes, and do you need real-time indexing for new docs?
03:11 - 03:45 Nadia: We do nightly bulk updates for most docs, but some new docs need to be available within a few seconds — so low-latency indexing for a subset.
03:46 - 04:20 Ethan: That lines up with a hybrid approach — many customers use prefix/BM25 for recall then Redwood does embedding-based rerank or a two-stage rerank. Do you have dimensionality constraints — like 128/256 vs 512/1536 — or are you flexible?
04:21 - 05:05 Priya: We're flexible but cost matters. Our current OpenAI embeddings are 1536 dims and that's working well for quality. We wanted to evaluate 512 or 384 to trade quality vs storage/ANN throughput. Any guidance?
05:06 - 06:00 Sofia: From a serving standpoint, lower dims reduce index size and speed up ANN queries — for HNSW, latency per query is roughly linear-ish with dimensionality and vector cardinality. If you're at ~10M vectors, 1536 dims is heavier; we often recommend 512 for production with quantization/OPS. Also Redwood can host embeddings generation or you can continue to send precomputed vectors; both supported.
06:01 - 06:40 Liam: If we switch to lower dims, do we risk hurting relevancy a lot? Our offline evals showed small drops for some query types.
06:41 - 07:20 Sofia: There's a tradeoff. Many teams see marginal drops at 512 that are acceptable given the cost savings, but it depends on your query distribution. We'll propose an eval plan in the benchmark template so you can compare recall/ndcg for 512 vs 1536 and also measure throughput.
07:21 - 08:05 Priya: Good. On the vector DB side, Pinecone is what we're on. We'd prefer to keep Pinecone as the index for now. Can Redwood integrate with Pinecone for retrieval and still do rerank in the Redwood runtime?
08:06 - 08:40 Sofia: Yes, we integrate with external vector stores. Two patterns: 1) Redwood performs embedding generation + sends vectors to Pinecone (so Pinecone is the single index), or 2) you keep Pinecone as the ANN store and Redwood calls out to Pinecone for candidate retrieval then runs rerank in the runtime — this keeps storage with Pinecone and uses Redwood for scoring. Both are common.
08:41 - 09:15 Nadia: Latency concern — calling out to Pinecone adds network hop. Does Redwood support colocated deployments or Private (VPC) to reduce that?
09:16 - 09:50 Sofia: Yes. For Hosted we have good regional endpoints; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower variability; Private (VPC/On-prem) lets you colocate with your Pinecone or self-hosted index. If you need sub-100ms 95th, Dedicated or Private is usually the right fit.
09:51 - 10:30 Ethan: And on the caching side, Redwood supports KV/prefix caching for repeated tokens which lowers cost/latency for chat-style flows; for embeddings rerank we support result caching for frequent queries too.
10:31 - 11:15 Priya: Can you run the rerank entirely inside Redwood with vectors stored in Redwood's internal store instead of Pinecone? That might reduce hops.
11:16 - 12:05 Sofia: Absolutely. You can push vectors into Redwood's internal index (we support ANN backends and sharded storage). The tradeoff is migration and operational ownership — Pinecone gives you a managed index you already trust. If latency is primary, putting vectors in the same deployment as the runtime helps.
12:06 - 12:50 Liam: What about hybrid search — BM25 + embeddings? We're using BM25 for recall now but want a fresher set of candidates for some queries.
12:51 - 13:30 Sofia: Hybrid is common: do an initial BM25/keyword pass (Elastic or your own) to get a recall set then use embeddings to rerank. Redwood supports both flows and can call your Elastic cluster or Pinecone as first stage, then do embedding scoring. We also have an integrated reranker pipeline to run local ANN + rerank.
13:31 - 14:05 Priya: How do you handle ANN index refreshes and consistency, especially for near-real-time indexing?
14:06 - 14:55 Sofia: For near-real-time, we use incremental indexing with small batches and background compaction. HNSW supports low-latency inserts but does have a compaction cost; we surface metrics and operators can tune refresh windows. With Dedicated you get predictable throughput so compactions are less disruptive.
14:56 - 15:35 Nadia: For throughput, in our worst-case loads we might spike to 200 qps for short bursts. Do you have autoscaling for Dedicated?
15:36 - 16:10 Sofia: Yes, Dedicated supports configured autoscaling and burst capacity. For strict SLOs we recommend a base reserved capacity sized for steady-state and then policies for bursts. We'll include a sizing worksheet.
16:11 - 16:50 Ethan: Let's talk about metric goals — Priya mentioned 95th under 200ms. Is that end-to-end from query to reranked response including Pinecone call?
16:51 - 17:30 Priya: Yes, that's end-to-end. For now 95th under 200ms is a hard requirement for search UX; we're flexible on the mean but 95th is critical.
17:31 - 18:10 Sofia: We'll design the pilot to measure end-to-end latency from your staging environment. If you give us Pinecone creds we can run the same queries and measure exact percentiles.
18:11 - 19:00 Liam: On security, we need SSO, SAML, audit logs, and if possible customer-managed keys for embeddings at rest. Can Redwood provide KMS integration if we go Private?
19:01 - 19:40 Ethan: Yes — Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging. Hosted offers encryption at rest and SOC2 controls; Dedicated adds VPC peering and tenant isolation. We'll attach the security datasheet.
19:41 - 20:20 Priya: Cost question — how do you price embeddings throughput vs inference? We need to model per-QPS cost.
20:21 - 21:00 Ethan: Hosted is pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved capacity with committed monthly. Embedding generation and queries are different line items — we'll share a pricing sheet and a calculator. For high QPS, Dedicated often gives better unit economics.
21:01 - 22:00 Nadia: Any guidance on dimensionality cost tradeoffs? e.g., 1536 -> storage and higher compute for ANN.
22:01 - 22:45 Sofia: Roughly speaking, index storage and ANN op cost scales linearly with dims and number of vectors. You can also use quantization (int8/4-bit) techniques; Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles that trade negligible quality for big storage savings. We'll include recommendations in the benchmark.
22:46 - 24:05 Priya: For our pilot, we want to compare 1536 vs 512, Pinecone external vs Redwood internal index, and Hosted vs Dedicated latency. Can you run that?
24:06 - 24:45 Sofia: Yes, that's a standard pilot. We'll run the same queries against both stores, measure recall/ndcg and latency percentiles, and provide cost estimates. We'll need a sample dataset and API keys to run tests.
24:46 - 26:00 Ethan: Quick question on reranker models — are you using a learning-to-rank model after embeddings or pure vector distance?
26:01 - 26:40 Priya: Currently pure cosine distance scoring on embeddings. We're experimenting with a small neural reranker but it's not in prod.
26:41 - 27:30 Sofia: Redwood supports configured scoring pipelines — pure vector, learned reranker, or hybrid. For a neural reranker we can host the small model in the runtime; that adds a bit of latency so we'll measure tradeoffs.
27:31 - 28:15 Liam: What telemetry do we get? Token-level cost isn't relevant here but we want per-route latency, error rates, and per-query logs for debugging.
28:16 - 29:00 Ethan: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, tracing, and you can export logs to your SIEM. We'll show examples in the deep dive.
29:01 - 31:00 Priya: One nit — sometimes transcripts call out KV "cash" instead of cache, ha. Anyway on governance, for Private deployments, can we run completely air-gapped?
31:01 - 31:40 Sofia: Yes — Private offers an on-prem package that can be air-gapped; it requires a different engagement and support SLA.
31:41 - 33:00 Nadia: For the Pinecone approach, is it possible to run Pinecone in our VPC or do we need to route through public endpoints?
33:01 - 33:40 Sofia: Pinecone offers a private endpoint option depending on your plan; alternatively, you can self-host a vector store like Milvus/ANN locally and Redwood can connect via VPC peering.
33:41 - 35:05 Ethan: We're nearing the end — wanted to confirm next steps and owners. Priya will share data and creds, we'll send the benchmark template, Sofia will size Dedicated options, and we'll schedule a kickoff.
35:06 - 36:00 Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? We just need to confirm legal for temporary creds — we try to keep keys scoped.
36:01 - 36:45 Ethan: Totally — scoped read-only creds are fine for benchmarking. We'll also send an NDA or addendum if needed.
36:46 - 38:00 Liam: Curious if Redwood has run similar pilots with other healthcare analytics companies — any references?
38:01 - 38:40 Ethan: Yes, we've done pilots with HelioHealth and other analytics firms; I'll include short references and case note.
38:41 - 40:10 Sofia: Quick technical note — for high QPS rerank you can enable GPU-backed serving in Dedicated which reduces latency for neural rerankers. We'll include GPU vs CPU cost estimates.
40:11 - 41:00 Priya: Great. For the benchmark, please include evaluation metrics (NDCG, MRR), latency percentiles, and cost per 1k queries.
41:01 - 42:00 Sofia: Will do. We'll also include guidance on dimensionality ablation and quantization profiles to try.
42:01 - 43:30 Nadia: One more question — do you support cosine vs dot product matching and how does that map to ANN backend compatibility?
43:31 - 44:10 Sofia: We support both; some ANN backends have optimized kernels for dot product, others for cosine (often implemented as normalized dot). We'll note compatibility with Pinecone, Milvus, and internal backends.
44:11 - 45:00 Ethan: Final wrap: we'll send the docs and pricing and try to get the pilot started next week. Thanks everyone.
45:01 - 56:00 [wrap-up, calendar scheduling, brief side conversation about billing contact — transcription quality medium, occasional mis-hearings like "KV cash" instead of cache and "Pine-cone" vs "Pinecone" spelled differently]

End of transcript.
